title: Introduction to Tailwind CSS
objectives: Explain utility-first styling and its trade-offs.
Compare traditional CSS, Bootstrap and Tailwind.
Describe matching-version Vite setup or use the preconfigured CodeLab compiler.
Build a simple utility-styled interface with visible focus.
introduction: Learn introduction to tailwind css through a sandboxed fictional school interface. Tailwind 4.3.3 is supplied locally; student JavaScript is isolated and no real backend is attached.
explanation: Utility-first CSS composes small styling classes directly in markup. Traditional CSS names semantic selectors; Bootstrap supplies opinionated component styles and plugins, whereas Tailwind utilities do not supply JavaScript behavior. Utilities speed composition but can create noisy repeated markup: extract components where useful. A playground/browser helper is convenient for learning, not the preferred production setup. This app already uses Tailwind 4.3.3 and @tailwindcss/vite; a real project imports Tailwind in its CSS and builds static output with the approved toolchain. The CodeLab practice compiler automatically supplies the same version, so setup boilerplate is unnecessary in every exercise.
syntax:
p-6: padding; max-w-md: limit width; rounded-xl: radius; text-2xl/font-bold: hierarchy; bg-indigo-700/text-white: button contrast; focus-visible:outline-2: keyboard focus.

Setup in this CodeLab: edit HTML and Run; the local 4.3.3 compiler is already provided. Do not paste a CDN script here.
External Vite practice project: inspect existing package versions first. If missing, install matching tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite packages. Add tailwindcss() from @tailwindcss/vite to the existing Vite plugins; import your CSS through the project entry; put @import "tailwindcss" in that stylesheet. Run the project's development command, then build static assets for production. Avoid adding a second version or rebuilding an existing app.
The official Play CDN/playground can illustrate quick browser learning in a separate disposable page. It is not the recommended production build. See tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/using-vite and /installation/play-cdn for version-aware procedures.

title: Spacing, Sizing, Colors, and Typography
objectives: Distinguish margin, padding and logical spacing.
Apply readable typography and color hierarchy.
introduction: Learn spacing, sizing, colors, and typography through a sandboxed fictional school interface. Tailwind 4.3.3 is supplied locally; student JavaScript is isolated and no real backend is attached.
explanation: Margin m/mt/mb/mx/my and logical ms/me utilities control outer space; padding p/px/py controls inner space. Logical start/end adapts to writing direction while ml/mr are physical. Width/height, min/max sizes and max-w-prose constrain content without fixed desktop assumptions. Text size/color, font weight, alignment, leading and tracking establish hierarchy. Border colors/width, rounded corners, shadows and opacity should clarify structure; low opacity can undermine contrast. Prefer a consistent scale.

title: Flexbox and Basic Layout
introduction: Learn flexbox and basic layout through a sandboxed fictional school interface. Tailwind 4.3.3 is supplied locally; student JavaScript is isolated and no real backend is attached.
explanation: Flex lays out one main axis. flex-row/flex-col choose direction; justify-* aligns along the main axis and items-* along the cross axis. flex-wrap prevents crowded content from overflowing, while nowrap can overflow small screens. gap sets consistent spacing, grow/shrink share or protect space and self-* overrides alignment for one item. Start with a mobile column and use md:flex-row for a wider layout. Visual order must not make keyboard/reading order confusing.

title: Grid and Responsive Design
objectives: Verify layout changes at actual viewport widths.
introduction: Learn grid and responsive design through a sandboxed fictional school interface. Tailwind 4.3.3 is supplied locally; student JavaScript is isolated and no real backend is attached.
explanation: Grid handles two-dimensional layout. grid-cols-* sets columns, gap controls spacing and col-span/row-span places larger regions. Unprefixed classes apply at every width; sm/md/lg/xl/2xl variants apply from configured minimum breakpoints upward. Mobile-first means a useful base layout before wider variants. Default v4 breakpoints are theme tokens and can be intentionally extended. Show/hide and responsive spacing are visual tools, not access controls.

Avoid showing every blank required field as an error before interaction in a real form.
